hazards.mechanism: A missing page or file is invisible because the incomplete subset happens to have a zero aggregate difference.
hazards.evidence: Verify report readiness, expected file count/sequence, page cursors, row count, checksums, and provider control totals before matching.
hazards.control: Fail the run as INCOMPLETE until the immutable source manifest proves the population is complete.
hazards.detection: Track gaps, duplicate sequence numbers, cursor loops, checksum changes, and manifest/control-total mismatches.
hazards.recovery: Reacquire the missing source under the same snapshot or start a new versioned run.
hazards.test: Remove the middle file from a three-file report while keeping compared aggregates equal.

hazards.mechanism: Systems compare different date meanings or timezones, especially across DST, and misclassify valid late or early records.
hazards.evidence: Name created, authorized, captured, available, settled, payout, and bank-booking dates plus timezone and cutoff for each source.
hazards.control: Select one documented date basis per control and normalize instants without discarding original local timestamps.
hazards.detection: Break out boundary exceptions by hour, timezone offset, and DST transition.
hazards.recovery: Re-run affected windows with corrected date mapping and preserve the superseded result.
hazards.test: Cover a DST fallback hour, month close, and a transaction captured before midnight but settled after it.

hazards.mechanism: A provider adds, reorders, removes, or reconfigures report columns and the parser silently shifts monetary fields.
hazards.evidence: Capture schema/report version, exact header order, required columns, type rules, and normalized mapping version.
hazards.control: Validate headers and schema fingerprints before ingestion; quarantine unknown or missing fields.
hazards.detection: Alert on schema hash changes, parse coercions, new journal types, and unexpected null-rate shifts.
hazards.recovery: Stop the run, version the parser, reingest raw files, and compare both normalized outputs.
hazards.test: Reorder fee/net columns and add an unknown journal type without changing the file name.

hazards.mechanism: Only internal-to-provider matching runs, so extra provider records or duplicate external effects remain invisible.
hazards.evidence: Inspect population counts and value coverage independently from both A-to-B and B-to-A directions.
hazards.control: Run double-sided matching and require every in-scope source record to end matched, explicitly excluded, or exceptional.
hazards.detection: Publish unmatched counts/value by source side and reason, never one blended percentage.
hazards.recovery: Classify the extra side, add missing internal evidence or reverse an unintended external movement.
hazards.test: Add a provider transaction with no internal request while every internal request still has a provider match.

hazards.mechanism: Duplicate source rows enter matching and make a valid one-to-one record look one-to-many or inflate totals.
hazards.evidence: Define source-record identity, file/version lineage, duplicate rules, and whether corrections reuse identifiers.
hazards.control: Deduplicate within an immutable staging layer before matching and quarantine conflicting duplicates.
hazards.detection: Count exact and conflicting duplicates by source identity and digest.
hazards.recovery: Exclude only by a recorded rule, preserve all raw rows, and rerun matches from staging.
hazards.test: Repeat an exact row and then repeat its ID with a changed amount.

hazards.mechanism: Amount-and-date matching chooses the wrong record when common values repeat or references are reused.
hazards.evidence: Measure candidate cardinality and the uniqueness of every composite rule over historical data.
hazards.control: Prefer stable financial IDs; classify any multi-candidate composite as AMBIGUOUS instead of picking nearest.
hazards.detection: Track candidates per match and rule-specific collision rates.
hazards.recovery: Undo the match decision without deleting evidence and resolve through stronger references or review.
hazards.test: Create two same-day, same-amount payments with a reused merchant reference.

hazards.mechanism: Fees, reserves, FX, refunds, chargebacks, and multiple captures are forced into one-to-one matches.
hazards.evidence: Map provider journal types and grouping identities to gross, fee, reserve, conversion, and net equations.
hazards.control: Support explicit one-to-many and many-to-one match groups with equation checks by asset.
hazards.detection: Report unmatched components and group equation residuals rather than hiding them in tolerance.
hazards.recovery: Reclassify the match cardinality, rebuild the group, and link any required ledger adjustment.
hazards.test: Match one payout containing captures, two refunds, a reserve adjustment, and fees.

hazards.mechanism: One source uses major units, another atomic units, or presentment and settlement currencies are compared as if identical.
hazards.evidence: Record source amount unit, scale version, gross currency, net/settlement currency, FX rate, and rounding component.
hazards.control: Normalize with a versioned asset registry and keep source amounts; compare only same-asset equations.
hazards.detection: Alert on 10x/100x/1,000,000x residual patterns and currency-pair mismatches.
hazards.recovery: Correct the normalization version and rerun from immutable raw sources; do not edit matches manually.
hazards.test: Mix major-unit CSV amounts, atomic-unit API amounts, zero-decimal currency, and FX settlement.

hazards.mechanism: A corrected or regenerated report is ingested as an additional population and double-counts the period.
hazards.evidence: Capture report identity, sequence, version, generation time, replacement semantics, and file digest.
hazards.control: Model report versions and supersession explicitly; never identify a source only by date.
hazards.detection: Alert when two source versions cover the same scope without a declared replacement relationship.
hazards.recovery: Supersede the old source in a new immutable run and reverse any adjustment caused solely by the old version.
hazards.test: Ingest version 002 after version 001 for the same settlement date and file sequence.

hazards.mechanism: Re-running a resolved exception posts the same financial adjustment again.
hazards.evidence: Trace exception identity, resolution decision, approval, adjustment operation key, ledger transaction, and verifying run.
hazards.control: Use a stable adjustment key derived from exception plus resolution version and post through the normal idempotent ledger path.
hazards.detection: Enforce unique adjustment keys and reconcile resolved exceptions to exactly one intended correction set.
hazards.recovery: Reverse the duplicate adjustment and link it to both the incident and original exception.
hazards.test: Replay the same run and resolution concurrently and require a single adjustment.
